moduleTitle: 2. Testing Throughout the Software Development Lifecycle
examDomain: Testing Throughout the Software Development Lifecycle
estTime: 130 min syllabus teaching allocation + retrieval practice (not a measured completion estimate)

topics.title: Official chapter 2 — Testing Throughout the Software Development Lifecycle

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Chapter keywords: explain, distinguish and exemplify

elements.text: These are original plain-language explanations, not quotations from the official glossary. For each term, give a new example and explain its difference from a neighboring term. Use the official glossary with the CTFL syllabus context for authoritative wording.

rows: acceptance testing
Evaluate readiness and suitability for business, user or operational needs, including contractual or regulatory expectations where applicable.
black-box testing
Derive tests from specified behavior without using the implementation structure as the basis.
component integration testing
Evaluate interactions and interfaces between components within a system.
component testing
Evaluate an individual component, often isolated from its collaborators.
confirmation testing
Check that a particular defect has been corrected.
functional testing
Evaluate what the product does against its functional expectations.
integration testing
Evaluate interactions between combined components or systems; distinguish the relevant integration level.
maintenance testing
Evaluate an operational product and effects of changes, migrations or retirement.
non-functional testing
Evaluate how well the product behaves, such as performance, usability or reliability.
regression testing
Look for adverse effects of changes in affected, connected or apparently unchanged areas.
shift left
Introduce useful testing and feedback earlier while retaining later evidence where needed.
system integration testing
Evaluate interactions of the tested system with other systems and external services.
system testing
Evaluate the complete system against its objectives and specification.
test level
A grouping of test activities defined by object, objectives, basis, typical defects and responsibilities.
test object
The particular component, interface, complete system or other artifact currently being tested.
test type
A grouping by the characteristic or purpose being assessed, independent of test level.
white-box testing
Derive tests using internal structure, such as statements and control-flow branches.

elements.text: Official exam weighting: 6/40 questions (15%). Work in short topic blocks; retrieve before rereading. The chapter quiz contains 20 original questions across all objectives of this chapter. Revisit high-confidence errors with Smart Review and use the full official chapter and keywords to check completeness.

elements.description: The lifecycle influences timing, scope, documentation, automation and roles. Sequential models often align levels with stages; iterative delivery repeats test activities within increments and needs growing regression coverage.

elements.text: Worked example: A team shipping weekly maintains regression automation while testing the new increment each week.
Close the notes: How would testing differ between a staged release and weekly increments?

elements.description: For each development activity use a corresponding test activity, define objectives for each test level, start analysis and design early, and involve testers in reviewing work products when drafts exist.

elements.text: Worked example: Draft requirements can be reviewed before development finishes even in a sequential lifecycle.
Close the notes: Recall good testing practices that apply across lifecycle models.

elements.description: TDD starts from component tests; ATDD starts from collaboratively agreed acceptance examples; BDD expresses desired behavior in a stakeholder-readable form, often Given/When/Then.

elements.text: Worked example: An acceptance example is agreed before implementing a user story. A unit assertion written first is a different test-first practice.
Close the notes: Distinguish TDD, ATDD and BDD by the test basis and participants.

elements.description: CI/CD and collaboration shorten feedback through automated builds and tests. Reliable environments and maintainable automation need investment; manual and non-functional testing remain useful.

elements.text: Worked example: A pipeline quickly catches a regression, while a tester still explores a newly designed workflow.
Close the notes: Which testing benefits and costs can a delivery pipeline introduce?

elements.description: Perform useful testing earlier: review drafts, analyze code and design tests before implementation. Shift left complements later system and operational testing rather than removing it.

elements.text: Worked example: Discussing an invalid input rule during refinement prevents a defect before the feature is coded.
Close the notes: Give an early test activity and a later activity that remains necessary.

elements.description: Inspect the process using evidence, agree actionable improvements, assign owners and follow up. Include successes as well as problems; evaluate actions in later iterations.

elements.text: Worked example: After repeated environment delays, a team assigns an owner to an automated environment check and reviews its effect next iteration.
Close the notes: Turn a complaint into a measurable improvement action.

elements.description: Component testing isolates units; component integration tests interactions between components; system tests evaluate the whole product; system integration tests interactions with other systems; acceptance evaluates readiness and stakeholder needs.

elements.text: Worked example: Testing a service against a stub is different from testing the deployed product against an external bank.
Close the notes: Classify five tests by their object, objective and basis, not their execution tool.

elements.description: Functional testing addresses what a system does; non-functional testing addresses how well it behaves. The syllabus lists performance efficiency, compatibility, usability (interaction capability), reliability, security, maintainability, portability (flexibility) and safety as non-functional characteristics. Black-box tests derive from behavior; white-box tests derive from structure. Levels and types are different dimensions.

elements.text: Worked example: A component performance check is non-functional testing at component level; a system price calculation check is functional.

headers: Non-functional characteristic in the CTFL syllabus
rows: Performance efficiency
A search finishes within its specified response-time limit under the stated load.
Compatibility
Two supported applications coexist and exchange information as required.
Usability / interaction capability
Representative users can complete the task and understand error feedback.
Reliability
The service recovers after an interruption and preserves the required behavior.
Security
An unauthorized user cannot read another account’s records.
Maintainability
A localized change can be analyzed, implemented and tested without unintended coupling.
Portability / flexibility
The supported deployment can move to another specified environment.
Safety
A hazardous condition is handled without exposing people or assets to the specified unacceptable harm.

elements.text: Use the characteristics listed in this syllabus edition. A correct exported total is functional evidence; the time required to export it is non-functional evidence. Either type may be checked at more than one test level.
Close the notes: Can non-functional testing occur below system level? Explain.

elements.description: Confirmation verifies that a reported defect has been corrected. Regression looks for harmful consequences of change, including in connected or unchanged areas. Both can occur at every level.

elements.text: Worked example: Rerun the failing invoice test to confirm the fix; test unaffected discount paths for regression.
Close the notes: Given two post-fix checks, identify their different objectives.

elements.description: Changes, migrations, environment upgrades and retirement can trigger maintenance tests. Impact analysis guides scope based on change risk, system size and change size; archived data may need retrieval tests.

elements.text: Worked example: Retiring an application still requires checking that legally retained records can be restored.
Close the notes: Why can retirement require testing even when no new feature is delivered?
Attempt these after studying the chapter, without looking at the keyword table. Explain each answer in your own words, then open the solution.

elements.title: Confirmation versus regression testing
elements.prompt: A defect in the discount calculation is fixed. Test A reruns the failing discount test. Test B reruns the tests for the checkout and invoice areas, whose code was not changed. Which is confirmation testing and which is regression testing?
elements.solution: Test A is confirmation testing: it checks that the original defect is fixed. Test B is regression testing: it checks that the change has not caused unwanted effects elsewhere. Regression tests are often good candidates for automation because they are run repeatedly.

elements.title: Test level versus test type
elements.prompt: A team runs performance tests during system testing and functional tests during component testing. Which terms are test levels, which are test types, and can every test type be used at every level?
elements.solution: System testing and component testing are test levels. Performance (non-functional) and functional testing are test types. Any of the four CTFL test types (functional, non-functional, black-box and white-box) can be performed at any test level, with a different focus at each level.

elements.title: Component integration versus system integration
elements.prompt: Test X checks the interface between the cart module and the pricing module of one application. Test Y checks the exchange between the application and an external payment service. Classify both.
elements.solution: X is component integration testing: interactions between components of one system. Y is system integration testing: interactions with other systems and external services.

elements.title: Maintenance testing triggers
elements.prompt: Which of these trigger maintenance testing: (1) a hotfix to production code; (2) moving the system to a new cloud platform; (3) retiring an application whose data must be archived; (4) testing the first release of a new system that is not yet in operation?
elements.solution: (1), (2) and (3). Modifications, upgrades or migrations of the operational environment, and retirement are maintenance triggers. (4) concerns a system that is not yet operational, so it is not maintenance testing.

examPitfalls.title: FL-2.1.1 · Lifecycle impact
examPitfalls.trapDescription: All test activities happen exactly once and only after all implementation is complete.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The lifecycle influences timing, scope, documentation, automation and roles. Sequential models often align levels with stages; iterative delivery repeats test activities within increments and needs growing regression coverage. Self-check: How would testing differ between a staged release and weekly increments?

examPitfalls.title: FL-2.1.2 · Lifecycle-independent practices
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Early analysis and work product review are practices restricted to Agile projects.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For each development activity use a corresponding test activity, define objectives for each test level, start analysis and design early, and involve testers in reviewing work products when drafts exist. Self-check: Recall good testing practices that apply across lifecycle models.

examPitfalls.title: FL-2.1.3 · Test-first development
examPitfalls.trapDescription: TDD, ATDD and BDD all use the same test basis and participants.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TDD starts from component tests; ATDD starts from collaboratively agreed acceptance examples; BDD expresses desired behavior in a stakeholder-readable form, often Given/When/Then. Self-check: Distinguish TDD, ATDD and BDD by the test basis and participants.

examPitfalls.title: FL-2.1.4 · DevOps and testing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A CI/CD pipeline removes the need for manual exploration, reliable data and maintenance.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: CI/CD and collaboration shorten feedback through automated builds and tests. Reliable environments and maintainable automation need investment; manual and non-functional testing remain useful. Self-check: Which testing benefits and costs can a delivery pipeline introduce?

examPitfalls.title: FL-2.1.5 · Shift left
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Shift left means eliminating later system and operational testing.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Perform useful testing earlier: review drafts, analyze code and design tests before implementation. Shift left complements later system and operational testing rather than removing it. Self-check: Give an early test activity and a later activity that remains necessary.

examPitfalls.title: FL-2.1.6 · Retrospectives
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A retrospective is complete when complaints are recorded, even without owned follow-up actions.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the process using evidence, agree actionable improvements, assign owners and follow up. Include successes as well as problems; evaluate actions in later iterations. Self-check: Turn a complaint into a measurable improvement action.

examPitfalls.title: FL-2.2.1 · Test levels
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Every integration test is system integration testing, even when it checks two internal components.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Component testing isolates units; component integration tests interactions between components; system tests evaluate the whole product; system integration tests interactions with other systems; acceptance evaluates readiness and stakeholder needs. Self-check: Classify five tests by their object, objective and basis, not their execution tool.

examPitfalls.title: FL-2.2.2 · Test types
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Non-functional testing is confined to the system level and white-box testing to components.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Functional testing addresses what a system does; non-functional testing addresses how well it behaves. The syllabus lists performance efficiency, compatibility, usability (interaction capability), reliability, security, maintainability, portability (flexibility) and safety as non-functional characteristics. Black-box tests derive from behavior; white-box tests derive from structure. Levels and types are different dimensions. Self-check: Can non-functional testing occur below system level? Explain.

examPitfalls.title: FL-2.2.3 · Confirmation and regression
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Confirmation and regression have the same objective because both occur after a change.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Confirmation verifies that a reported defect has been corrected. Regression looks for harmful consequences of change, including in connected or unchanged areas. Both can occur at every level. Self-check: Given two post-fix checks, identify their different objectives.

examPitfalls.title: FL-2.3.1 · Maintenance testing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A migration or retirement needs no testing unless a new business feature is added.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Changes, migrations, environment upgrades and retirement can trigger maintenance tests. Impact analysis guides scope based on change risk, system size and change size; archived data may need retrieval tests. Self-check: Why can retirement require testing even when no new feature is delivered?

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team moves from annual releases to weekly increments. What testing change is particularly relevant?

options.text: Replacing all acceptance tests with a release checklist
Repeated testing of increments with maintained regression coverage
Deferring every test activity to an annual stabilization phase
Reducing testing to the newly changed source lines

practiceQuiz.rationale: Frequent increments need testing of new behavior and potential side effects. Deferred testing, checklist replacement and changed-line limits miss important risks.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does a sequential lifecycle affect test preparation?

options.text: Reviewing requirements becomes a maintenance activity
All testing work must wait until the whole product runs
Component testing becomes unnecessary
Tests can be analyzed and designed alongside corresponding development artifacts

practiceQuiz.rationale: Executable tests may run later, but preparation and reviews can start early. The lifecycle does not eliminate component testing or redefine reviews as maintenance.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which practice applies across development lifecycles?

options.text: Use the same test documents on every project
Execute acceptance tests before requirements are drafted
Avoid reviews until the last iteration
Start test analysis and design during the corresponding development phase

practiceQuiz.rationale: Early analysis and design are broadly useful. Identical documents and an imposed sequence ignore context; delayed reviews lose early feedback.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What should be defined for each test level?

options.text: A fixed identical number of cases
A mandatory separate external supplier
Specific test objectives
A ban on automation

practiceQuiz.rationale: Objectives guide test work. Separate suppliers, equal counts and automation bans are not general good-practice requirements.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which approach typically writes component tests before the code they exercise?

options.text: Test-driven development
Exploratory testing
Checklist-based testing
Maintenance testing

practiceQuiz.rationale: TDD starts from a failing component test. The alternatives do not define that development cycle.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which phrase most directly identifies a common BDD example format?

options.text: Plan, Do, Check
Given, When, Then
Arrange, Budget, Release
Open, Assign, Close

practiceQuiz.rationale: Given/When/Then expresses context, event and expected behavior. The other sequences do not identify the BDD scenario format.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is a testing benefit of CI in a DevOps environment?

options.text: Guaranteed equivalence of every environment
Removal of the need to investigate failed checks
Earlier feedback from automated build and regression checks
Elimination of non-functional testing

practiceQuiz.rationale: Pipeline automation shortens feedback. Investigation, non-functional assessment and environment control remain necessary.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A pipeline has many flaky checks. What is a sound response?

options.text: Investigate and maintain their reliability before relying on results
Treat every red result as evidence of a product defect
Delete the checks without assessing the covered risks
Treat every green result as release authorization

practiceQuiz.rationale: Unreliable automation needs investigation. Red may reflect infrastructure, green is limited evidence, and deletion can remove needed coverage.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which action most clearly illustrates shift left?

options.text: Performing production monitoring after release
Reviewing acceptance examples before implementation
Waiting for full system availability to design tests
Moving the final regression run to a different server

practiceQuiz.rationale: Earlier prevention and feedback illustrate shift left. Infrastructure relocation and later monitoring do not shift a test activity earlier.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does successful shift left imply for later testing?

options.text: System tests can be removed once requirements are reviewed
Every test must execute before source code exists
Operational risks are proven absent by static analysis
Later tests remain necessary for risks detectable in integrated behavior

practiceQuiz.rationale: Earlier techniques complement later ones. Integrated and operational behavior cannot all be assessed before execution is possible.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A retrospective identifies repeated late test data delivery. What is the best next step?

options.text: Stop collecting evidence about data delays
Record the complaint with no follow-up owner
Assign an improvement action and review its effect next iteration
Blame the data author in a public report

practiceQuiz.rationale: A retrospective should produce follow-through and learning. Blame and passive recording do not address the process problem.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which evidence best indicates a retrospective action helped?

options.text: The meeting lasted longer than the prior meeting
The action was added to a slide
Comparable subsequent iterations show reduced environment waiting time
Everyone agreed that retrospectives are useful

practiceQuiz.rationale: Evaluate the intended outcome using relevant evidence. Meeting length, documentation and agreement do not demonstrate the effect.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test checks interaction between the product and an external bank system. Which level is most appropriate?

options.text: System integration testing
Component testing
Component integration testing
An isolated unit test

practiceQuiz.rationale: The boundary crosses systems. Component integration concerns components within a system; component/unit tests isolate smaller objects.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Business users evaluate whether a complete product supports their workflows. Which level is this?

options.text: Static code analysis
Component integration testing
Component testing
Acceptance testing

practiceQuiz.rationale: Acceptance evaluates readiness and needs. The alternatives address lower-level interactions, isolated units or static structure.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A service is tested for response time at component level. How is this classified?

options.text: Functional testing at system level
Static testing because the scope is small
Acceptance testing by definition
Non-functional testing at component level

practiceQuiz.rationale: Type and level are independent. Response time is non-functional, and execution makes the test dynamic regardless of object size.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test checks the specified refund amount without examining implementation. Which description fits?

options.text: White-box branch testing
Functional black-box testing
Static syntax analysis
Non-functional load testing

practiceQuiz.rationale: Specified business outputs provide a functional black-box basis. Structure, syntax and load are different test bases or objectives.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After a tax fix, a tester checks the original wrong-tax case. What is the primary objective?

options.text: Risk transfer
Effort estimation
Confirmation
Regression in unrelated features

practiceQuiz.rationale: The original defect is being checked for correction. Regression targets adverse consequences; risk transfer and estimation do not describe this test.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After a tax fix, a tester checks an unchanged invoice export. What is the primary objective?

options.text: Regression
Static requirement review
Confirmation of the tax defect
Release planning

practiceQuiz.rationale: The unchanged behavior may suffer side effects. That is regression; confirming the original defect would target the failing tax case.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A database is migrated without changing business features. Is testing relevant?

options.text: No, a new feature is required to trigger testing
Yes, conversion and environment changes can trigger maintenance tests
Yes, but tests must exclude unchanged behavior
No, migrations are exclusively a project management concern

practiceQuiz.rationale: Migration introduces product risks, including conversion errors and regression in unchanged areas. New features are not required.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A retired system's records must remain retrievable for seven years. What should be tested?

options.text: Archiving, retrieval and restoration behavior
The deprecated UI color scheme alone
The former team's staffing ratio alone
New feature prioritization for that system

practiceQuiz.rationale: Retirement may create retention and recovery risks. Staffing and obsolete presentation checks do not address access to archived data.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the objective and apply the decision rule to the facts before comparing alternatives.
